jobs.occupation: Senior Systems Engineer - Electric Propulsion (all genders) (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description: ABOUT THE ROLEAs Senior Systems Engineer – Electric Propulsion, your mission is to ensure that the electric propulsion system is fit for its intended purpose, enabling aircraft-level performance, safety, and certifiability throughout the aircraft lifecycle.With deep expertise in electric propulsion, you connect system requirements, system design, supplier deliverables, and verification into a consistent technical baseline. You drive technical trade-offs, resolve complex system issues, and ensure that interfaces, operating modes, and constraints remain aligned with the aircraft’s concept of operation and neighbouring systems.Working closely with engineering teams, suppliers, and safety and certification specialists, you ensure that the propulsion system is ready for integration, ground and flight testing, and entry into service. You provide clear technical recommendations and evidence to support informed decisions at system and aircraft level.WHAT YOU WILL DO• Own a complete, consistent, and traceable requirements baseline for the electric propulsion system, translating aircraft, safety, certification, and programme needs into system and equipment requirements.• Define and maintain the system architecture, interfaces, operating modes, and constraints, including the interaction of electric motors, inverters, and propulsion controls• Drive system-level trade studies and recommend architecture and design solutions, making assumptions, technical risks, and open issues transparent and resolving or escalating them with a clear assessment of their impact.• Define validation and verification strategies and coordinate evidence closure across system, subsystem, and equipment levels, ensuring coverage of all allocated requirements and readiness for certification milestones.• Lead technical discussions with suppliers and engineering partners, aligning requirements, interfaces, deliverables, and acceptance criteria against a shared technical baseline.• Assess the impact of proposed design changes on requirements, interfaces, verification, safety, certification, and configuration, coordinating the assessment with affected stakeholders before implementation.• Prepare system engineering deliverables for technical reviews, integration, ground and flight testing, and service readiness gates, providing clear status, evidence, deviations, and residual risk assessments.WHAT YOU BRING• An engineering degree or equivalent qualification in aerospace, electrical, systems, control engineering, or a related discipline.• Extensive systems engineering experience with complex technical products.• Deep technical understanding of electric propulsion systems, including electric motors, inverters, propulsion controls, and their electrical, thermal, and mechanical integration.• Experience in aviation or a comparably regulated industry, such as space, automotive, or defence.• A strong command of requirements engineering, traceability, technical baseline management, and the assessment of design changes.• The ability to lead technical discussions across disciplines and with suppliers, evaluate competing solutions, and turn complex issues into well-supported recommendations.• Strong analytical judgement and self-management, with a proactive approach to technical risk, issue resolution, and stakeholder alignment.• Professional working English for technical documentation and stakeholder communication.WHAT WE OFFER• Full-scale aerospace engineering, not concept slides• A 60+ engineer team at Ottobrunn• Real ownership and flat hierarchies: a modern startup culture where your input shapes decisions, not just execution• Flexible working hours, remote work, and competitive compensation• Health & wellbeing: EGYM Wellpass membership and subsidized lunch in our canteen• Office extras: espresso coffee, fresh fruit, and soft drinks, plus regular team and company events, and plenty more once you're on boardAbout usclick here!Built for purpose.When time matters.ERC was founded to close Europe's critical capability gap in the sky. Two full-scale demonstrators. Two EU records. Built for the missions that cannot wait.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher “Molecular Mechanisms of Musculoskeletal Diseases” (m/f/d) (Molekularbiologe/-biologin)
jobs.description: The position is located at the Department of Trauma and Orthopedic Surgery, University Hospital Erlangen, within the research group Musculoskeletal Inflammation in Traumatology, led by Prof. Jana Riegger-Koch. Our research focuses on the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying musculoskeletal diseases, particularly osteoporosis, impaired fracture healing, and age-related and post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Two central research pillars are the complement system and its role in inflammation and tissue degeneration, and cell fate decisions in response to cellular stress and injury, including differentiation, senescence, and cell death. We aim to translate these mechanistic insights into novel therapeutic strategies for tissue protection and regeneration. More information: www.riegger-lab.de ( https://www.riegger-lab.de/ )Your tasks- Contribute to ongoing research projects and (co-)supervise students- Independently plan, perform, and analyse laboratory experiments- Optimise existing protocols and establish new experimental methods- Contribute to laboratory management and coordination of technical staff- Participate in teaching activities, including practical courses and lectures- Present research findings at national and international scientific conferences- Prepare scientific manuscripts and contribute to grant applicationsQualifications- PhD in life sciences, such as molecular medicine, biology, or a related discipline- Strong background in musculoskeletal diseases, mitochondria, immunology, and/or molecular biology- Hands-on experience in cell culture techniques, fluorescence microscopy, molecular biological techniques (e.g., qRT-PCR, siRNA transfection, and others), Western blotting, and/or histology- Excellent written and spoken English skillsAdditional advantages- Experience in bioinformatics, omics technologies, or single-cell analysis- Experience in supervising students, preparing grant applications, or working with We offer a PhD position in the research group of Dr. Frederik Kotz-Helmer, which is embedded within the NeptunLab led by Prof. Bastian E. Rapp at the Department of Microsystems Engineering (IMTEK), University of Freiburg. NeptunLab is a highly interdisciplinary research environment focusing on the development of novel materials, manufacturing technologies, and processes for industrial applications. Research from the NeptunLab has been published in leading international journals, including Lab on a Chip, Advanced Materials, Angewandte Chemie, and Nature, and has received attention from national and international media outlets such as the BBC, The New York Times, and the Discovery Channel.Glass is an essential engineering material for applications ranging from optics and photonics to microtechnology and high-performance components. However, conventional glass manufacturing technologies strongly limit the geometries that can be produced and often require complex and energy-intensive processing routes.Within this PhD project, a novel extrusion-based manufacturing technology for glass will be developed. The approach is based on highly filled thermoplastic nanocomposites containing silica nanoparticles dispersed in a polymeric binder system. These materials are shaped in the polymeric state by extrusion and subsequently converted into dense, transparent glass through debinding and sintering.A major focus of the project will be the development of thermoplastic nanocomposites with tailored rheological and mechanical properties. Polymer composition, molecular weight, particle loading, particle dispersion, and processing conditions will be systematically investigated to establish relationships between material formulation, flow behavior, extrusion stability, and the geometry of the resulting components. Structured extrusion dies will be used to directly manufacture complex cross-sectional geometries, providing a new route toward continuous manufacturing of structured glass components.The successful candidate will work at the interface of materials science, polymer processing, rheology, nanocomposites, and glass technology. The project combines fundamental materials research with the development of a new manufacturing process and therefore provides substantial freedom for both scientific investigation and technology development.Developing highly filled thermoplastic silica nanocomposites for extrusion-based glass manufacturing.Designing polymer binder systems with tailored rheological, mechanical, and debinding properties.Developing and optimizing extrusion processes for complex and microstructured geometries.Investigating the relationship between extrusion parameters, die geometry, material flow, and dimensional accuracy.Designing and evaluating structured extrusion dies for the continuous manufacturing of complex glass components.Characterizing nanocomposites and glasses using techniques such as SEM, XRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, rheology, thermal analysis, and optical characterization.Establishing quantitative material-process-structure relationships for extrusion-based glass manufacturing.Presenting research results at international conferences and publishing findings in peer-reviewed journals.Master’s degree/Bachelor’s degree/Studies in Material Science, Mechanical Engineering, Process Engineering or related subjectsProfound knowledge of polymer chemistry, material science and processing is requiredKnowledge of glass science, ceramic processing or polymer extrusion are/is beneficial.Excellent academic track recordExcellent English skills in reading and writingYou should be a team player with ambitions who can conduct research projects independentlyYou should be able to structure and document your work properlyYou should be a creative mind without causing excessive chaos around youAn interdisciplinary work environment with a team of motivated scientists that strive to develop clever solu...
